Unique Background & Feats
The Path into the Wilds
Ever since you could take your first steps, you heeded the call to wander. 
Each distant horizon only promising more to explore. Nothing and no one 
could hold you back and you have learned to sustain yourself in the primal 
wilds, living off the land and thriving. You are a Traveler, and home is the 
welcoming crackle of a warm fire under the stars.
Ability Scores: Constitution, Dexterity, Wisdom
Feat: Primal Scavenger
Skill Proficiencies: Perception and Survival
Tool Proficiency: Maker's Kit (pg. 247)
Equipment: Fishing Rod, Explorer's Pack, Hand Axe, Iron Pot, 
Quarterstaff, Tent, Traveler's Clothes 
Sol'Kesh Feats
Primal Scavenger
Skilled Harvester You roll with Advantage when Scavenging a 
creature for Components (pg.246).
Weathered You have Advantage against any weather related 
hazard Saving Throws.
Origin Feats
Wild Kin • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Wisdom 13+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Wisdom score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Kin Points You have access to Kin Points which you can spend 
to gain Advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks. Your 
maximum amount of Kin Points are equal to your Wisdom 
Modifier and you regain your expended Kin Points when you 
finish a Long Rest. 
Feral Trust • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Charisma 12+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Natural Rider You have Advantage on checks made to control or 
guide a mount.
Protective You can use your Reaction to redirect an attack that 
targets your mount to yourself instead, as long as you are within 
5 ft. of your mount.
General Feats
Wayward • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Dexterity 13+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Bound to the Soil Choose one type of biome: Coastal 
(Strands), Desert/Fields/Mountains (Farplains), Forest/Jungle 
(Wealdwoods), Swamp/Wetland (Fenlands), or Underdark/
Subterranean (Umbrawells). You gain Proficiency in the Stealth 
skill of the chosen biome, and you can move at normal speed while 
moving stealthily.
Natural Chef • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Constitution 11+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Skilled Cook Add + 1 Bonus Modifier to the Meal Preparation roll. 
(pg. 245)
Wild Artisan • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Intelligence 12+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Skilled Craftsmen Add + 1 Bonus Modifier to the Crafting roll (pg. 247)
Epic Boon Feats
Wilderheart Boon • Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Wisdom score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Earthborne Instincts You can use your Wisdom modifier instead 
of your Intelligence modifier when making Nature checks,
True Traveler You gain Proficiency in: Nature, Perception, Stealth, 
and Survival.
Boon of the Harvester • Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Living off the Land Add ±1 to the range result for Hunting, 
Foraging, Setting Snares and Fishing Expeditions.
Boon of the Tamer • Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+)
Ability Score Increase Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Steady Hand Automatically fill 1 Tamed Segment when beginning 
to Tame a creature.
Hunters Sense • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+,Wisdom 10+) 
Beast Sense You have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks 
related to Tracking, and can recognize a creature’s scent and 
distinguish it from others once you’ve interacted with it or its 
tracks in the past.
On The Trail Beasts have Disadvantage on Stealth checks made to 
hide from you, if you’ve tracked them within the last hour.
Unyielding • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Constitution 10+) 
Ironwood Stance When you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or 
Slashing damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce the damage 
by your Proficiency bonus.
Protector When an ally within 5 ft. takes damage, you can use 
your Reaction to move up to 5 ft. toward them without provoking 
Opportunity attacks.
Skilled Scaler • General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength 10+) 
Ability Score Increase Increase your Strength score by 1, to a 
maximum of 20.
Strong Grip You gain a climb speed equal to your walking speed. 
If you already have a climb speed, increase it by 10 ft..
Wall Leap As a Bonus Action, if you are adjacent to a vertical 
surface (such as a wall or cliff face), you can leap off the surface and 
jump up to half your movement in any direction. This movement 
does not provoke Opportunity attacks.
Solo Play & Narrative Leads
Storytelling is the key to role playing games and a Traveler can explore their own story without the need of a Keeper to tell it. The 
following pages provide methods to explore the island of Sol'Kesh in Solo Play. Either by adventuring alone into the wilds, creating NPC 
animals and allies to accompany you, or to simply add a narrative goal to pursue. In addition, these tools can also provide a Keeper with 
more storytelling tools to tell a story for their adventuring Travelers.
Journaling
The heart of Sol'Kesh is exploration, to discover uncharted lands 
and observe beasts in their natural habitat. A Traveler is more than 
just an adventurer, they are explorers, researchers, pioneers and 
more. As a Traveler experiences Solo Play, it is recommended that 
they keep a journal of their adventures. Not only does it include 
the benefits of the Journal Feature (pg. 248) it helps solidify the 
events that they experience, to note the progress they made in 
discovering new life, and help map out their exploration of the 
island itself.
Journal Example
Third day of Spring's waning moon - 
That old tattered recipe book I found in that beached ship wasn't wrong, 
when gathering dropmoss, bring a ladder. I spent the better part of the 
morning swatting flies that flew up from the Mirewynn the moment I left 
that blessed dry patch of dirt that was my campsite. Like a wall of green, 
the Tanglewood greeted me, and while the early morning sky was already 
bright with sunshine, all of the optimism that comes with that came to a 
grinding halt as I stepped into that gloom under the trees. I think I even 
startled a frondilli when I stepped on a branch a little too loudly...All I 
saw was a green furred tail disappear into the bush. After what felt like 
hours of walking, I finally spied that telltale gray moss hanging heavy 
of the boughs dozens of feet above me. With an audible sigh that I soon 
regretted once I remembered there's more than frondilli in these woods, I 
got to climbing. Thankfully my master's lessons in looping rope around 
the trunk still held merit, and before long I was high into the canopy and 
starting to remember the feeling of sunlight on my skin. That moment of 
peace was quickly forgotten as the tree began to shake. I could suddenly 
feel a steady deep thud coming from the distance and immediately worried 
that I was in the path of the Tanglewood's resident apex predator, an old 
grizzled jhotus. All the birds flying off away past the source was a warning 
I was not too foolish to ignore. Quickly cutting off a healthy bundle of the 
moss I descended with less grace than I want to admit, and immediately 
ran out of those woods, not wanting to take my chances with the terrifyingly 
huge jhotus catching my scent.
Expeditions and Environments
Within the pages of this book can be found the means to explore 
a myriad of encounters and daily quests. A Traveler can choose 
to begin their adventure by selecting from the Job Board (pg. 
257). Can choose an area on the Island Map (pg. 9) or roll on any 
of the five Biome's Expedition Tables, to either Forage, Hunt, Set 
Snares and Fish, or simply venture out and risk their survival in 
the primal wilds.
When experiencing Solo Play and embarking on any of these 
potential adventures, it is recommended for a Traveler to roll 
on the Biome's Weather Table per day of travel, and roll on the 
Scavengers Table per biome for every hour in the wilds, as the 
roaming hungry predators are always on the look out for a meal 
and the randomness of nature can lend a level of danger and 
variation to the session.
Beastly Behavior
The creatures that call Sol'Kesh home are more than mindless 
encounters and are meant to naturally coexist within their 
environment. Not all creatures are out to rip apart a Traveler 
savagely, and in many cases fear the strange intruder. When 
encountering a creature in Solo Play, a Traveler can roll on the 
Beast Behavior Table (pg. 256) to determine how the creature will 
react to their presence, as each creature has a listed behavior type 
in how they react to a Traveler.
The Path Taken
While some may want to forge ahead entirely alone on this island 
of savage beasts, journeying through Sol'Kesh in Solo Play does 
not necessarily mean the Traveler must do so alone and unaided, 
and can involve Non Playable Characters (NPCs) along the way to 
aid a Traveler on their quest. Below is a list of potential narrative 
plots that could help add substance and story to your path. Yet the 
most important tool in your kit will always be your own creativity. 
• Add NPC characters taken from 5e's Monster Manual, from 
Commoners, Scouts, Warriors to Cultists. Give these characters 
a name and consider a backstory of why and how they are on the 
island with the Traveler. If they're lucky, they may survive a whole 
season in these wilds.
• Fast forward the process of Taming a creature and add a 
wayward beast to the Traveler's side immediately. Perhaps an 
orphan vinnirex chanced upon them when they washed ashore, 
or protective skyelarx spied them from afar and is guarding over 
them and their perilous journey.
• The Traveler is part of a crew that came across these uncharted 
coasts in a vessel fitting exploration, whether from across the 
waves in a ship or across the stars in a spelljammer ship. Together 
they venture out on expeditions to discover the lay of the land.
• Sol'Kesh is merely a newly discovered island within an existing 
fantasy world, people have flocked to its shores to set up a colony 
of sorts. Through hardship and grit they have built a community 
to grow and call this island a new home. 
• Eschewing all fantasy magic, the Traveler is a human from our 
modern Earth and has skipped forward in time to 82 millions 
years to the distant future. Alone and completely cut off from the 
remains of humanity, they must survive in this new era far from 
the modern world they once knew.
